text: Nasdaq 100 futures fell more than 2% and S&P 500 futures about 1.3% after a Reuters report that the US could announce new tariffs on 16 major trading partners.
The VIX jumped about 15% to 30.26 from Tuesday's 26.36 close, and bitcoin slipped 2.6% to about $58,653.
October PCE prices rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, matching forecasts, while core prices rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% forecast.
Spot gold slipped about 1% to around $3,518 and big gold miners fell 1.5% to 3.9% before the open, with GDXJ down 1.7% in pre-market trading.
Silver fell another 1.4% to $40.26, pushing the gold/silver ratio up to 87.64.
QQQ traded at $624.01 before the open, down 2.2%, while SQQQ was up 7.4% at $52.26.
Brent eased about 0.5% to near $91 on worries about a supply glut ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting.
USD/JPY held near 159.25 as hot Japanese services inflation and intervention worries kept the yen steady.
